source.note: The source is this repository's own Python implementation, not a second checkout. Cadenza is being rewritten in place (cadenza#8): `src/cadenza/` and `tests/` are the specification until a later PR retires them, so every inventory here is collected from the working tree at the recorded revision.

suite_baseline.reconciliation: `PYTHONPATH=src PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` at a5672f8 on CPython 3.12.3: 330 passed. No module is skipped at collection time, so collected == the sum of the eight per-file inventories with nothing left over. See parity/source-inventory.manifest.json.

file.note: 6 test functions, 62 collected node ids: `test_refuses_each_documented_ref_violation` alone contributes 23, and the git-parity corpus contributes another 24 by construction.

systematic_mappings.to: `expect(() => parseBaseBranch(value)).toThrow(expected)`, where `expected` is a plain string (substring match, which is what every source `match=` pattern reduces to once it carries no regex metacharacter beyond a literal escaped dot) or, in the three rows whose pattern is exactly that escaped dot, a `RegExp` built from the same characters
systematic_mappings.why: `InvalidBaseBranchError.message` already carries the formatted `"<detail> (at <location>)"` text (design doc's one shape change from Python, recorded at `src/domain/errors.ts`), so `str(exc)` and `.message` are the same string and no adaptation was needed there. What changed is the assertion's own vocabulary: vitest's `toThrow(string)` is `.includes()`, not `re.search`. For every row except the two ref rules whose `match=` is itself a regex (`r"must not contain '\.\.'"`, `r"must not end with '\.lock'"`), the two are the same check by construction. Those two carry a `RegExp` built from the same characters rather than a plain string transcribed from the regex source (DECISIONS.md D-0021): the source pattern's only metacharacter is an escaped, literal dot, so a plain substring of the rendered text -- which `pythonRepr` prints with two literal dots and no backslash -- would also have been correct, but transcribing the pattern's own backslashes into a plain string would not be, and a `RegExp` removes the choice rather than relying on reasoning it through by hand each time.
systematic_mappings.affects: all 23 cases of 'refuses each documented ref violation'

systematic_mappings.why: Recorded once at D-0018 rather than per case: `True` has no direct TypeScript analogue distinct from `1`, so the port represents it as the JavaScript `boolean` `true` and relies on `pythonTypeName` to print `bool`, and `None` as `null` relies on it to print `NoneType`. The source only asserts the substring `must be a string, got`, not the printed type name, so this mapping is not itself pinned by any case in this file -- it is pinned in `test/domain/python-semantics.test.ts`, which is target-only.
systematic_mappings.affects: all 4 cases of 'refuses non-string values naming the type'

systematic_mappings.from: `shutil.which("git")` at import time, and `@pytest.mark.skipif(GIT is None, ...)` on the parametrized function
systematic_mappings.to: `gitAvailable()`, spawning `git --version` once via `node:child_process.execFileSync` and catching ENOENT, then `test.skipIf(!GIT_AVAILABLE)(...)` applied inside a loop rather than to a single decorated function
systematic_mappings.why: pytest's `skipif` marker decorates the whole parametrized test once and every generated case inherits it; vitest has no equivalent that composes with `testkit/parametrize`'s shared id-preserving helper, so this one group is written as a plain `for` loop calling `test.skipIf` per case instead. The loop is one call site in the source text -- `scripts/parity-check.mjs`'s non-running sweep is syntactic, not a runtime count -- so it is approved once in `target.approved_non_running` regardless of how many of the 24 cases the loop produces.
systematic_mappings.affects: all 24 cases of 'the validator refuses everything git refuses'

systematic_mappings.to: `gitAcceptsBranchName(name)`: the same `git check-ref-format refs/heads/<name>` invocation via `execFileSync`, with a non-zero exit caught and turned into `false` rather than read off a `returncode` field
systematic_mappings.why: `execFileSync` throws on a non-zero exit instead of returning a status code, which is the one shape difference from `subprocess.run(check=False)`; the question asked of the process -- did `git` accept this ref name -- is identical, and neither invocation goes through a shell.
systematic_mappings.affects: all 24 cases of 'the validator refuses everything git refuses'

target_only_tests.why: Every test in this file translates a source case.

approved_non_running.reason: One `test.skipIf(!GIT_AVAILABLE)` call site inside the loop that ports 'the validator refuses everything git refuses' (24 source cases), mirroring the source's own `@pytest.mark.skipif(GIT is None, reason="git is not installed")`. It runs the 24 cases normally wherever `git` is on PATH -- true in this repository's own dev environment and in CI -- and skips them together, rather than failing, on a machine without `git`. Counted once because the check reads the syntax tree, not the loop's 24 runtime iterations.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: The git-parity corpus (`PARITY_CORPUS`) is 24 branch-name shapes chosen by the source file to exercise every rule the validator makes a decision about, not an exhaustive search of `git check-ref-format`'s own behaviour.
inherited_limitations.why: The source's own shape, recorded there as "the point of the corpus is that git, not this file, says what the answer is" -- a claim about direction (never more permissive than git), not about coverage. Carried over unchanged rather than widened, because widening the corpus is a decision about the source file's own scope and belongs to whichever belt owns `tests/test_refs.py`, not to this translation.

inherited_limitations.behaviour: 'the validator refuses everything git refuses' and 'the shapes codex review found' skip -- entirely, not merely report inconclusive -- on a machine with no `git` on `PATH`.
inherited_limitations.why: The source's own shape: `@pytest.mark.skipif(GIT is None, ...)` does the same. `git` is present in this repository's own CI images and dev containers, so the skip is not expected to fire there; it is inherited rather than tightened because CI's binary environment is not this belt's to decide.

entries.target_id: test/domain/refs.test.ts::parse_base_branch > refuses each documented ref violation[main..dev-must not contain '\\.\\.']
entries.reason: Same assertion: `..` is refused. Adapted rather than covered by the file-wide substring mapping: the source's own `match=` is a regex (`r"must not contain '\.\.'"`) whose only metacharacter is an escaped, literal dot, so matching it as a plain substring in TypeScript would search for a backslash the thrown message never contains -- `pythonRepr` prints two literal dots. A `RegExp` built from the same characters is used instead, which is the one case where the mechanism genuinely has to stay a regex rather than collapse to `.includes()`.
